jobs.description:
We store summer sun for the winter. Now Photoncycle is heading into thousands of Danish homes, and we are looking for a trainee who wants to help build the market from the ground up. Is that you?

About Photoncycle

Solar panels produce plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that problem: we store the energy in a tank in the ground next to the house, so the household can use it for electricity and heating all winter. Surplus power is sold on the electricity market, where it helps balance supply and demand. The household pays a fixed monthly fee, and we build, install and operate the system.

We are 25 employees with offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026 we raised a €15 million Series A led by NordicNinja and Voima Ventures. We are now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, and the first phase of our production plant is underway.

Photoncycle is a completely new technology, and Denmark is our first market.

Why this role

As a trainee, you will be part of building Photoncycle's Danish operations, from research and permit processes to partner dialogues, pilot customers and events. You will work across the full breadth of a market launch and get hands-on experience with how a new energy technology is brought to market in Denmark.

The role is deliberately broad, and the scope will be tailored to the number of hours you work. Tasks will shift as the launch gets closer, and your responsibilities will grow with the role down the line.

What you will do

This is a versatile, hands-on role that mixes research, relationships and the nuts-and-bolts work. You will report to Anne Clara Laugesen, General Manager of Photoncycle Denmark, and work closely with our colleagues in Oslo.

Tasks and responsibility will include:

Market build and operations support

• 
Support our pilot customer programme, from first contact to onboarding

• 
Follow and assist with permit processes and dialogues with municipalities and authorities

• 
Help build and maintain relationships with customers, partners and stakeholders

• 
Take part in preparing test sites and the first installations

Research and analysis

• 
Desk research on municipalities, funding schemes, partners and competitors

• 
Monitor funding and grant opportunities

• 
Collect and structure data and recurring customer questions for internal use

Events and meetings

• 
Practical planning of customer meetings, community events and site visits: invitations, sign-ups, venue, catering and follow-up

• 
Prepare material and logistics for conferences and external events the team attends

What you bring

We imagine you being structured and comfortable juggling many small tasks at once. You take ownership, spot what needs to be done, and ask when something is unclear.

We expect you to:

• 
Be studying, or recently graduated, in a relevant field such as business, energy, engineering, public administration or similar

• 
Write and speak Danish fluently and work comfortably in English

• 
Be confident with Office tools and quick to pick up new systems

• 
Handle confidential information, including customer data, with care

It is a plus if you:

• 
Have an interest in the energy transition, energy systems or the Danish energy market

• 
Have experience from a startup, student job or association work with admin or coordination

• 
Are used to working with AI tools

You don't need to be an energy expert. What matters most is that you enjoy building something new where the right answer isn't known yet – so apply even if you can't tick every box.

What we offer

• 
A front-row seat to building a new energy company in Denmark ahead of a 2027 launch

• 
Close daily collaboration with the GM and real responsibility from day one

• 
Insight into regulation, permits, partnerships and go-to-market in the energy sector

• 
A small, international team with colleagues in Norway

• 
An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BloxHub, with a great lunch setup and free coffee

Start and application

The position can be set up in three ways: as a paid student job (15–37 hours a week), as an internship as part of your studies, or as virksomhedspraktik via your jobcentre if you have recently graduated and are currently unemployed. Hours and tasks are tailored to the arrangement. The start date is yesterday – or whenever you're ready, really.

We will be taking interviews as applications come in.

Photoncycle is committed to an inclusive workplace and hires based on skills, experience and potential. We encourage everyone interested to apply, regardless of gender, age, ethnic background, religion or disability.

We look forward to hearing from you!

SYBO is part of the Miniclip family and known for the widely popular game, Subway Surfers - the most downloaded mobile game in the world, with over four and a half billion downloads. Located in the heart of Copenhagen, we aim to create playful moments that inspire our fans to care.

_Some games chase trends. Subway Surfers helped define an entire genre.

_Now, we're looking for a UI/UX Designer to help shape what comes next.

This is your chance to leave your mark on one of the biggest mobile games ever made. A game with a massive global audience, instant player feedback, and a team that never settles for "good enough". The challenge? Keeping an iconic game feeling fresh, modern, and innovative for hundreds of millions of players around the world.

Come help evolve the visual experience of Subway Surfers, designing new features, game modes, and player journeys while continuously improving the experience that keeps players coming back. Some days you'll be crafting entirely new interfaces. Other days you'll make a tiny change that unlocks a surprisingly big impact. That's the fun part.

If you enjoy solving creative puzzles, have a knack for details, and seeing your work reach millions of players, then this might just be your gig.

**Responsibilities

**

• Actively refine and improve existing UI/UX to elevate player engagement and satisfaction, ensuring Subway Surfers remains intuitive, modern, and enjoyable to play.

• Design and implement intuitive, engaging UI screens, assets, and interactions for new and existing features.

• Create UX wireframes, user flows, and prototypes to support feature development and player experiences.

• Help shape the visual direction of the game's interface, evolving and modernizing the experience, while staying true to the Subway Surfers brand.

• Ensure a consistent visual style, tone, and user experience across all UI elements.

• Create and maintain UI documentation, design systems, and style guides to support consistency and scalability.

• Optimize UI implementations to ensure smooth performance across a wide range of mobile devices.

Life at SYBO

**In your first month...

**You'll get to know the team, the game, and the players that have made Subway Surfers one of the most successful mobile games in the world. You'll be introduced to our tools, workflows, and ways of working while building relationships across the studio. With support from your teammates, you'll begin contributing to your first projects and quickly find your footing as part of the team.

**Within 3 months...

**You'll start taking ownership of more impactful work across the game, designing engaging interfaces and helping improve the player experience through thoughtful UI/UX solutions. You'll collaborate closely with the team to iterate on designs based on player feedback, insights, and performance data.

**By 12 months...

**You'll be a trusted contributor to the future of Subway Surfers, able to lead individual UI/UX initiatives across major features. At this point, your contributions to the UI style guide and visual framework will have enabled a smoother collaboration across teams, ensuring Subway Surfers will remain an evergreen.

**Requirements

**

• A strong portfolio demonstrating solid UI design work for games, with clear examples of creating intuitive, polished, and engaging player experiences.

• Strong ability to create wireframes, user flows, mockups, and polished final designs that effectively balance player needs and business goals.

• Skilled at designing, rendering, and animating high-quality UI elements that bring personality and clarity to the player experience.

• Advanced proficiency with modern UI/UX and prototyping tools, particularly Figma.

• Experience working with Unity and a solid understanding of UI implementation

Bonus Points

• Knowledge of conducting user research and translating player insights into actionable design improvements.

• Experience working on large-scale live service mobile games.

**About SYBO

**We're SYBO, the mobile games studio behind the legendary Subway Surfers, with over 4.5 billion downloads worldwide! Join our team in the heart of Copenhagen, where creativity flourishes in our new, state-of-the-art studio.

If you join us, you'll have the opportunity to dive into exciting and creative projects alongside a diverse group of like-minded colleagues from over 40 countries across the globe.

We truly believe you perform your best, when you have the equipment you need - and our IT team is always on hand to ensure you have access to the latest tools and gear, enabling you to be at your best - even remotely with a home-office budget!

We also pride ourselves in taking care of your well-being, offering a delicious lunch buffet, a variety of healthy snacks, and regular social events to keep the energy flowing.

Not in Copenhagen? Not a problem! We have in-house relocation specialists who will help you relocate, and feel right at home in Copenhagen and at SYBO!

SYBO is committed to providing equal opportunities to all applicants, regardless of race, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

A senior legal role with genuine influence

Fertin Pharma is looking for a Senior Group Legal Counsel who combines strong legal judgement with commercial perspective and the confidence to advise at executive level. You will be entrusted with complex, high-impact matters where the legal path is not always defined—and where your ability to set direction, balance risk and opportunity, and turn complexity into decisive advice will directly influence business outcomes.

Reporting to the VP, Head of Legal, Regulatory and QA, you will operate as a senior individual contributor and legal owner across key business areas. Although the role has no direct line management responsibility, it carries a clear functional leadership mandate: you will shape legal strategy, challenge and support senior stakeholders, lead cross-functional initiatives and set standards for how Legal enables the organisation.

Your mandate

• Strategic legal leadership: Develop and implement legal strategies and risk mitigation frameworks for key business areas, aligned with Fertin’s business objectives, group requirements and legal risk appetite.

• Executive and senior stakeholder counsel: Provide expert, commercially pragmatic legal advice to senior management and cross-functional leaders on complex legal, commercial, regulatory, governance and reputational matters.

• Commercial contracts and business support: Own the legal strategy, negotiation approach and risk position for material commercial agreements, including customer, supplier, development, manufacturing, licensing and strategic collaboration arrangements.

• IP and confidential know-how: Lead the legal framework for protecting Fertin’s IP, know-how and confidential information in commercial and R&D collaborations, including ownership, access rights, confidentiality and contractual protections

• Compliance/GDPR: Lead and implement legal compliance and data protection frameworks in relevant areas, including GDPR, confidentiality, sanctions, third-party risk and group policies, in coordination with PMI Legal where relevant.

• Regulatory, quality and product-related legal matters: Act as legal owner for strategic input into regulatory, quality and product-related matters, identifying legal risks and developing practical solutions across functions and jurisdictions.

• Corporate governance: Develop and implement governance processes, powers of attorney, corporate approvals, board/management documentation and internal legal policies to support clear decision-making and accountability.

• Disputes and claims: Lead the legal handling of disputes, claims and settlement strategies, including legal assessment, risk exposure, negotiation strategy and coordination with external counsel.

• Group and intercompany matters: Support legal structuring and documentation for intercompany arrangements, intra-group services and group governance matters, ensuring clear responsibilities and alignment with business, tax and Finance stakeholders.

• Legal processes, templates and standards: Develop and improve legal processes, contract standards, templates, playbooks and ways of working to strengthen quality, efficiency, consistency and risk management across the organisation.

• AI adoption in Legal: Lead responsible use of AI tools within Legal, including identifying use cases, setting governance principles and ensuring confidentiality, quality and legal risk controls.

The senior profile we are looking for

• You hold a Master of Laws, cand.jur., cand.merc.jur. or an equivalent legal qualification.

• You bring at least five years of relevant experience from an international in-house legal function and/or a law firm, with a track record that demonstrates senior-level judgement and ownership.

• You have substantial experience with sophisticated commercial agreements and legal risk management; experience within compliance, governance, IP or regulated industries will be a strong advantage.

• You are comfortable operating where matters are complex, cross-border or ambiguous, and you know when to decide, challenge, involve others or escalate.

• You can move confidently between strategic advice and hands-on execution—from executive counsel and negotiation strategy to drafting, implementation and follow-through.

• You communicate with authority and clarity, build credibility quickly and can influence stakeholders without relying on formal management authority.

• You are commercially pragmatic without compromising legal integrity, and you are motivated by building solutions and standards that last.

Your impact

This role offers the opportunity to influence decisions close to the business, own matters of strategic importance and leave a visible mark on how Legal operates across Fertin Pharma. Your success will be reflected not only in sound legal outcomes, but also in stronger decision-making, clearer risk ownership and legal frameworks that enable the organisation to move forward with confidence.

Interested?

If you are an experienced legal professional who wants more than a traditional advisory role—and are ready to take ownership, influence senior stakeholders and shape the legal agenda in an international and highly regulated environment—we would like to hear from you.

Special Conditions

As part of our recruitment process, we conduct background checks on all candidates who accept an offer of employment with Fertin. A satisfactory background check is a condition of employment.

The background check is a standard and important part of our hiring process and is carried out in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, as well as Fertin’s internal compliance and integrity requirements.

Do you have a passion for robotics and automation? And would you like to see the solutions you work with come to life at customer sites around the world?

At Inwatec, we develop and build advanced automation and robotic solutions for industrial laundries worldwide. We are looking for a Software Commissioning Engineer who enjoys combining software, robotics, and hands-on problem solving.

You will work closely with our engineers in Denmark, but a big part of your job happens where our solutions are put into action: at customer sites around the world.

YOUR TASKS

• Programming and configuring robots, machines PC and PLC systems

• Testing and commissioning systems at customer sites

• Implementing our automation solutions worldwide

• Troubleshooting software, PLC, network and machine-related issues

• Fine-tuning systems to ensure stability and performance

• Supporting customers during installation and start-up by being the ”Face on-site”

• Being co-responsible in cutomer teaching of our system during training and meetings

• Working closely with our software team to improve existing solutions and develop new features through feedback from site

YOUR PROFILE

• You have a degree in robotics, automation, software, engineering or a similar technical field

• You have an interest in programming, robotics, and industrial automation

• You enjoy hands-on problem solving, and seeing your solutions work in the real world

• You are curious, independent, and comfortable taking responsibility on-site

• You are fluent in English and confident communicating with customers and colleagues internationally. Additional language skills, particularly German or French, are an advantage

• Previous experience with PLCs, robotics, commissioning or industrial machinery is an advantage, but not necessarily a requirement

• You have a category B driver's license

• You are excited about travelling. The position includes approximately 100–150 travel days per year, primarily for commissioning at customer sites worldwide

WE OFFER

• A job where you combine software, robotics, and real-world engineering

• The opportunity to follow solutions from testing in Denmark to full operation at customer sites

• International experience through projects around the world, involving travel from a few days to a couple of weeks, and occasionally longer trips with the possibility of a break along the way

• A high degree of responsibility and freedom in your work

• Skilled colleagues within software, automation, and engineering

• Good opportunities to develop both your technical and personal skills

• An informal working environment with short decision-making processes

One week you might be testing a system in Denmark. The next, you could be commissioning a robot on the other side of the world.

If that sounds like the kind of engineering job you are looking for, we would like to hear from you.

INWATEC - THE LAUNDRYNERDS

JENSEN-Group is a global leader in industrial laundry technology, with roots on Bornholm and a strong developmental focus. Inwatec ApS is part of JENSEN-GROUP, and Inwatec develops and produces machines and robots for industrial laundries worldwide. We are a fast-moving company in rapid development and our team is creative and dynamic, with very dedicated employees. We love our informal work environment, where every idea is taken seriously and everybody is treated equally. On Fridays, we meet at our bar for an after-work beer or some ping-pong.

We are looking forward to moving into beautiful new offices on Hvidkærvej, Odense in 2027.

**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we're saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**Experience Design transforms complex financial workflows into intuitive solutions that drive measurable business outcomes. We bridge sophisticated investment technology with the people who depend on it — portfolio managers, compliance officers, and analysts operating in high-stakes environments where precision and speed matter.

Our Global Experience Design team operates as a centralized center of excellence with distributed impact. We maintain unified standards and processes globally while embedding designers directly within product teams for deep collaboration and contextual expertise. This lets us stay consistent across SimCorp's product ecosystem while scaling expertise efficiently across markets and time zones.

As Principal Experience Designer, you will serve as the senior design authority for our most complex, strategic initiatives, influence design direction across multiple teams, and mentor senior designers.

At SimCorp, we support some of the largest financial institutions in the world to be successful by simplifying their investments, accounting and operations.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Lead design for SimCorp's most complex and strategic initiatives, contributing to the overall strategic vision and design craft excellence.

• Establish design patterns and standards adopted across the organization, and influence design system evolution and adoption.

• Drive innovation in financial technology user experience, influencing multiple products across the organization.

• Partner with senior product leadership on roadmap planning, and represent the design perspective in architectural and technical decisions.

• Act as a thought leader and subject matter expert in UX.

• Work closely with engineering leadership on technical feasibility, and collaborate with user research on strategic research initiatives.

• Partner with customer success to integrate user feedback, and present design vision to executive stakeholders.

• Work independently and cross-functionally with senior leadership.

• Mentor Lead and Senior Experience Designers, and contribute to hiring decisions for senior design roles.

**What We Value

**Most importantly, you can see yourself contributing and thriving in the position described above. How you gained the skills needed for doing that is less important. We expect you to be good at several of the following and be able to — and interested in — learn the rest.

• 8+ years of design experience, with deep expertise in enterprise software.

• Proven track record leading complex, multi-team design initiatives.

• Strong systems thinking and design pattern recognition.

• Ability to navigate between high-level strategy and detailed execution.

• Skill in translating complex financial concepts into clear, actionable interfaces.

• Experience getting the most from AI tools in crafting creative solutions.

• Experience mentoring senior designers and design leaders.

• Ability to facilitate cross-functional collaboration and drive stakeholder consensus.

• Self-directed and results-oriented, taking ownership of projects while contributing to our collective design practice.

• Experience with the fintech domain is a plus.

**Benefits

**Attractive salary and bonus scheme are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide a good work and life balance: flexible working hours and a hybrid model - working from SimCorp's office two days a week. And opportunities for professional development: there is never only one route - we offer a personal approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take. Visit our career pages to learn more about working at SimCorp.

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually. At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway.

SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

SimCorp welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Candidates who require accommodation during the recruitment process should contact the People & Culture team at PeopleandCultureAmericas@simcorp.com.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, without regard to race, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

Please note: Only applications sent through our system will be processed.

For New York City only: The salary range for this position is $160,000 - $241,000 USD. Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including health care, leave, and retirement plans. Your total compensation may vary based on role, location, department and individual performance.

Are you the kind of person who notices when something could be better, and has the drive to make it happen? At DISA, quality is not just a checkpoint at the end of the process. It is built into the way we design, source, produce and deliver world-class foundry machines. We are looking for a Quality Engineer who wants to be close to the product, close to production and close to the decisions that improve how we work.

This role is for someone who enjoys solving real quality challenges in a manufacturing environment. Someone who is structured, curious and persistent enough to follow an issue from first observation to sustainable improvement.

What You’ll Do

• Take ownership of quality improvements across supplier quality, production quality and internal quality processes.

• Handle non-conformities, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and ensure follow-up until issues are properly closed.

• Work closely with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers to identify risks, solve quality challenges and prevent repeat issues.

• Support and develop supplier quality performance through audits, structured follow-up, documentation and improvement plans.

• Use data, facts and structured problem-solving tools to analyze trends, set priorities and recommend practical quality improvements.

• Contribute to audits, customer requirements and management systems, with ISO 14001 as an area where you have basic knowledge or interest.

Why You’ll Love Working with Us

• A role where quality is at the center — not a side responsibility.

• The chance to work hands-on with complex, high-precision equipment and see the impact of your improvements in real production.

• A workplace where your structure, curiosity and follow-through help prevent issues before they reach the customer.

• Close collaboration with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers, so you can turn observations into practical improvements.

• The opportunity to help strengthen quality culture in a global industrial company with strong products, proud craftsmanship and long product lifetimes.

You will not be sitting far away from the product or the people making it. You will be part of the daily dialogue around quality, helping colleagues and suppliers understand what went wrong, why it happened and how we make sure it does not happen again.

Who You Are

• You have a background in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Production Technology or a similar field.

• You have experience with quality work in a manufacturing, production or industrial environment.

• You are motivated by root cause analysis, corrective actions and the satisfaction of closing issues properly.

• You understand supplier quality or are eager to work closely with suppliers on deviations, audits, documentation and improvement plans.

• You like being close to the shop floor and working with people across functions to solve practical quality challenges.

• You are analytical and structured, but also pragmatic enough to find solutions that work in real life.

• You follow through — because you know that quality improvements only matter when they are actually implemented and sustained.

• You have knowledge of ISO 14001 or an interest in building a basic understanding of environmental management systems.

If you are driven by quality, manufacturing and continuous improvement, and if you enjoy turning problems into clear actions and better ways of working, we would like to hear from you. You do not need to tick every box; what matters most is your quality mindset, your curiosity and your ability to follow through.

About Norican

NORICAN. Metal. Made. Possible.

We are Norican, a global industrial group designing, building and supporting best‑in‑class machines and technologies for metal formation and surface treatment.

Bringing together five leading brands - DISA, Simpson, StrikoWestofen, Wheelabrator and Monitizer – we deliver one connected solution across the production process, supported by full‑service expertise and digital solutions.

Across green sand molding, die casting, sand preparation, melting, transport and dosing, and surface treatment, we help manufacturers improve performance and transform production across a wide range of industries. We build lifetime quality and long‑term partnerships by combining the strengths of our legacy brands to lead the industry through innovation, sustainability and profitable growth.

DISA:

DISA design, build and support premium green sand moulding and cashing machines for the ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industries. For 125 years they have delivered machines that last for decades, and they are highly respected by customers and peers for excellent levels of quality and service. DISA machines keep customers producing relentlessly to the very highest standards. And they empower foundry productivity with a lifetime of efficient and a lower cost per casting.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

We will review candidates continuously, so please send your application as soon as possible. If you have any questions about the role, please contact Johnny Rasmussen at johnny.rasmussen@norican.com.

jobs.occupation: Technical Lead - Substation Automation and Communication Systems
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with automation and communication systems for high-voltage substations? Can you lead technical work packages and coordinate specialist contributions to deliver an integrated solution? Join COWI as our new Technical Lead and contribute to the development of Denmark’s electricity transmission infrastructure.

Take technical responsibility for substation automation projects

We are looking for an experienced engineer to take technical responsibility for substation automation and communication systems in high-voltage substation projects. You will work on projects ranging from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites. You will coordinate specialist contributions, manage technical interfaces and ensure that individual work packages meet the requirements of the overall substation automation solution.

The role combines technical expertise with responsibility for coordinating engineering activities, monitoring progress and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables. You will work closely with the project manager, technical specialists and other engineering disciplines throughout project execution.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead and coordinate the technical delivery of substation automation and communication systems.

• Plan and follow up on engineering activities, technical deliverables and milestones within your scope.

• Coordinate specialist contributions and ensure consistency across technical work packages.

• Ensure that technical solutions and documentation comply with project requirements, customer specifications and applicable standards.

• Manage technical interfaces between automation, communication systems, protection systems, primary equipment and auxiliary systems.

• Identify and resolve technical issues in collaboration with specialists and other engineering disciplines.

• Participate in project meetings and advise the project manager on technical matters, dependencies and risks within your area of responsibility.

• Coordinate technical activities with customers, suppliers and other project stakeholders.

Your expertise

You combine a strong technical foundation with a structured approach to planning and coordination. You can assess how individual systems and specialist contributions fit together, communicate technical requirements clearly and follow through on agreed actions.

You work independently and build effective working relationships with colleagues, customers and project partners.

You will also bring:

• A degree in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical qualification, together with more than five years of relevant experience in automation for high-voltage substations.

• A solid understanding of substation automation systems, including control and monitoring functions, communication networks and interfaces to protection equipment.

• An understanding of how substation secondary systems interface with high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience coordinating technical work packages, planning engineering activities and following up on specialist deliverables.

• The ability to assess technical solutions, manage interfaces and maintain an overview of quality, progress and dependencies.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• The ability to obtain the required security clearance and fulfil the requirements for the designated on-site role of “holdleder” at high-voltage substations.

Your place of work

Depending on project requirements, you may work from one of COWI’s offices in Denmark, at Energinet project locations or partly from home. Travel within Denmark is expected.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Head of Discipline Carsten Sass Husum at CSHU@COWI.COM.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Equal opportunity employer

COWI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, COWI complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

STUDIO 9 is looking for a commercially driven Sales Manager to turn strong customer interest in KEYSTONE into signed contracts and long-term partnerships.

This role carries clear responsibility for the sales pipeline and the full commercial process, from initial customer dialogue and pilot to negotiation and agreement.

ABOUT KEYSTONE

KEYSTONE is STUDIO 9’s SaaS platform that enables our customers to collect, structure and manage product data directly from their suppliers.

The platform makes it easier for our customers to meet the evolving compliance requirements in areas spanning from EUDR, supply chain traceability, digital product passport (DPP) and LCA. It is built as a SaaS platform that can easily integrate into our customers’ system landscape (e.g. to their ERP and PIM-system).

ABOUT THE ROLE

Working closely with our Sales Director and Software & Implementation team, you will drive KEYSTONE’s commercial growth and help shape how the platform is positioned, sold and delivered.

You will lead the customer journey from the first conversation through agreement, onboarding and long-term development. This includes identifying the right decision-makers, building support across the customer’s organisation and presenting a clear financial and operational case for choosing KEYSTONE.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Drive customer acquisition and commercial growth for KEYSTONE

• Own the sales process from initial dialogue to signed agreement

• Progress opportunities through demonstrations, pilots, negotiations and internal approvals

• Identify decision-makers and build support across the customer’s organisation

• Build compelling ROI cases that demonstrate KEYSTONE’s financial and operational value

• Maintain a structured pipeline with forecasts and clear next steps

• Ensure a smooth transition from sales to implementation

• Support customer adoption, retention and account growth

• Bring customer insights into product positioning and business development, collaborating closely with Sales, Product and Software teams

ABOUT YOU

You are motivated by progressing sales opportunities and turning interest into lasting customer relationships. You work in a structured way, create momentum and follow opportunities through to completion.

You are comfortable exploring a customer’s software landscape, understanding how systems, data and workflows connect, and translating software capabilities into clear business value. You can engage both commercial and IT stakeholders in conversations about business needs, integrations and scalability.

You bring:

jobs.occupation: Technical Workstream Lead - Procure to Pay 1
jobs.description:
Own the technical backbone for your workstream. As the Technical Workstream Lead for Procure to Pay you sit side-by-side with the Global Process Owner (GPO) and Global Process Leads (GPLs) to translate process design into robust and scalable technology across ERP, PLM, QMS procurement system solutions. You lead the technical scope for your workstream - architecture, build, environments, integrations, data migration, non-functionals, security/compliance, releases, and hyper-care – through stage gates to successful handover.

Ambu is transforming our core enterprise platforms (e.g., ERP, QMS, PLM), and each workstream needs a dedicated technical leader to ensure high-quality, compliant delivery that enables standardized, high-performing global processes.

**The role

**You are the end-to-end technical owner for one workstream. You co-lead the workstream together with the Business Workstream Lead/GPO, ensuring process-system alignment, decision-ready design, disciplined delivery, and operational readiness for your scope.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• 
Technical governance within your workstream

• 
Run technical governance for the workstream. Prepare decision-ready design packs and status for the Design Authority

• 
Own the workstream technical enablement of the Procure to Pay process. Assess run-time/architecture risks, define mitigations, and escalate with clear options

• 
Safeguard solution integrity against enterprise standards and non-functional requirements

• 
Design, build, environments, and release engineering

• 
Lead technical design for your workstream: integrations, extensions, data model, security roles, automation

• 
Define and manage environments for the workstream: branching strategy, CI/CD pipelines, and code quality gates

• 
Manage technical debt, versioning, and change control with impact analysis across upstream/downstream systems

• 
Data migration and cutover

• 
Plan and execute migration tooling, trial loads, reconciliations, and cutover steps for your workstream objects

• 
Security, privacy, and compliance

• 
Ensure cybersecurity, privacy, SoD, and validation/CSV compliance in collaboration with QA/Validation Lead

• 
Delivery orchestration and hyper-care

• 
Coordinate internal platform teams and external vendors for your scope

• 
Lead hyper-care triage and stabilization for the workstream. Complete documentation and knowledge transfer to run

• 
Program collaboration

• 
Partner daily with the GPO, GPLs, and Business Workstream Lead; align on scope, decisions, and adoption

• 
Work with PMO on stage gates, quality reviews, plans, and dependencies to other workstreams

**Your profile

**

• 8+ years delivering technical workstreams on enterprise platforms (ERP, QMS, PLM or similar) in global settings

• Proven leadership of architecture, integrations (API/iPaaS), data migration, and release management within a defined scope

• Strong command of non-functionals: performance, reliability, security, privacy, SoD, and validation/CSV

• Hands-on experience with CI/CD, environment strategy, branching, automation testing, and code quality

• Adept at partnering with GPOs/GPLs to translate future-state processes into scalable solution designs

• Skilled in vendor management and cross-team coordination. Clear, concise communicator in English

• Willingness to travel across Ambu’s footprint and collaborate across time zones

**Nice to have

**

• MedTech/life sciences background (GxP, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 11, CSV)

• Exposure to Infor M3 or equivalent ERP, plus PLM, QMS, iPaaS/data platforms, and modern security frameworks

• Experience with Agile-at-scale combined with stage-gate governance

**Key stakeholders for your workstream

**

• Global Process Owner and Global Process Leads

• QA/Validation Lead

• PMO

• External implementation partners and software vendors

**Key Responsibilities Following The Transformation

**

• Participate in approved global projects

• Provide advice for standard systems and best practices of ERP and related systems

• Act as Service Delivery Manager and Subject Matter Expert in ERP in the IT Application Team

• Configure and maintain ERP systems, ensuring alignment with business requirements and best practices.

• Handle system configuration, unit testing, training, and documentation in accordance with standards in close cooperation with external partners.

• Manage Life Cycle Management & release management

• Coach and review work performed by peer professionals

• Work across functions and cultures to deliver high-quality global solutions

• Work independently to solve complex problems

• Train Business Process Owners and other key users

• Follow regulatory compliance

**Ambu – where your technical leadership matters

**Join a fast-growing, international company where your workstream leadership directly enables how we operate globally. We offer strong professional development and a competitive package of professional, social, and financial benefits.

**How To Apply

**Send your CV and a short note describing a program where you led the technical workstream for a specific domain from design through hyper-care, including how you de-risked integrations, data migration, and non-functionals.

FPRT is looking for a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for our new composite production in Vojens, Denmark, and Moment Professionals manages the recruitment on our behalf. We are looking for a composite specialist with real depth in the technology who can convert transferred know-how into controlled, scalable and repeatable industrial processes. The role suits you if you want to build a production from the ground up and would rather build processes where little is written down yet than step into a production where everything is already in place.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

And then there are the benefits:

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

• Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is a strong advantage, or the willingness to learn it.

It is an advantage if you:

• come from advanced composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence, pressure vessels, automotive or another high-performance application.

• have worked with large or structurally critical components, such as aerospace and defence structures, casings, filament-wound products, UAV components or wind turbine blades.

• have taken part in a greenfield factory, a new production line, a technology transfer or a major ramp-up.

• live within commuting distance of 6500 Vojens, Denmark.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

Job Description:

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with wind turbine drivetrains or comparable large rotating machinery is preferred. Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. We also welcome specialists who want to broaden their understanding of the complete drivetrain.

What can you look forward to?

You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

About Goldwind

Goldwind Energy ApS (also called Goldwind Denmark) is a R&D focused subsidiary of GOLDWIND SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. (Goldwind), a world leading wind turbine technology and energy solutions provider headquartered in Beijing, China.

Through the implementation and investment in industry-leading turbine technology, water treatment solutions and other green energy technological ventures, Goldwind has been hailed as one of China’s most innovative companies.
